messages:
sara: FYI customer (acme-bio) on private cluster in eu-west reported GPUs failing after a kernel update tonight. jobs get stuck at first token and some pods show nv_peer_memory errors.
ryan: Which kernel and driver versions did they move from/to? did they update the nvidia package too?
sara: They said kernel bumped 5.15.0-70 -> 5.15.0-72, driver remains 530.41.03 per their ops. dmesg shows "nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout" and some NCCL socket errors.
maya: That module_layout message → classic kernel module ABI mismatch. Likely kernel updated but nvidia module wasn't rebuilt against new headers. Ask them for `modinfo nvidia` and `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version`.
jon: Also have them run `dkms status` and check `ls /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel/drivers/video/ | grep nvidia`. If DKMS didn't run or headers missing, module won't load.
sophia: Short-term: can they boot back to the old kernel from grub? If not, workaround (if headers present) is `sudo dkms autoinstall` then `modprobe nvidia`. For NCCL net issues try `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS` or pin `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` to avoid failing interfaces.
ops-bot: rolling-update: hostgroup private-eu-west maintenance window 03:00-05:00 UTC — rollback allowed during window.
sara: They said they can't reboot for ~48h. Any non-reboot options?
ryan: If headers exist we can rebuild in-place (`dkms autoinstall`) without full reboot, but unloading/loading nvidia modules mid-run will kill any running processes. There's also kpatch/livepatch but module ABI mismatches won't be fixed by that. CPU fallback is possible but will blow cost and latency.
jon: I'll assemble a customer-facing supported matrix (kernel <> driver <> required dkms/headers) and a one-line remediation per cell. Example commands to include: 
```
# check
uname -r
modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic
dkms status
# remediate (if headers installed)
sudo apt-get install linux-headers-$(uname -r)
sudo dkms autoinstall
sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia
sudo update-initramfs -u
```
maya: Also add the `vermagic` check — if `modinfo nvidia` vermagic != `uname -r` then rebuild is required. Collect `dmesg | grep -i nvidia` too.
sophia: Ops suggestion: require DKMS + kernels headers in onboarding for private installs. We should also add a lightweight health probe that reports `dkms status` + vermagic to the console so we surface drift earlier.
sara: Can you include these exact log commands for the customer? They specifically asked "what supported matrix do you guarantee for private installs".
jon: Will draft a short matrix and remediation doc and post to #docs and ping you. ETA ~4h.
sara: :thumbsup: thanks — I'll keep the customer updated and ask them to paste the `dmesg` and `dkms status` outputs here when available.
